findings.explanation: The PR relocates SearchResultSerializer from views.py to serialisers.py and drops the PassUserMixin base class in the process. In the base snapshot, `class SearchResultSerializer(DocumentSerializer, PassUserMixin)` (views.py:817) inherited PassUserMixin, whose get_serializer passes `user=self.request.user` and `full_perms` into the serializer (views.py:210-216). The new class in the PR is `class SearchResultSerializer(DocumentSerializer)` with no PassUserMixin (serialisers.py:799). Because DocumentSerializer extends OwnedObjectSerializer -> SerializerWithPerms, the serializer's to_representation depends on the `user` kwarg to compute object-level permission fields (e.g. user_can_change) and to respect `full_perms`. Removing PassUserMixin means the serializer no longer receives the request user, so permission-aware output is lost/incorrect. This is a changed line (the new class definition) that newly exposes the serializer to be used without the user context, weakening the authorization-aware representation of documents.

evidence.content: By default, the API will return a truncated version of object-level permissions, returning `user_can_change` indicating whether the current user can edit the object (either because they are the object owner or have permissions granted). You can pass the parameter `full_perms=true` to API calls to view the full permissions of objects.

findings.suggested_fix: Preserve the user-passing behavior when relocating the serializer. Either keep PassUserMixin in the new SearchResultSerializer base, or ensure the view that instantiates this serializer (e.g. GlobalSearchView / UnifiedSearchViewSet) passes `user` and `full_perms` into the serializer so object-level permission fields are computed correctly.
